title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned Riso Zine. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.
channel: Crush question form with pictures (owner's standing preference: look choices in the form, no pop-up pages)
ownerWords: while I do think the general design is good, it does look too generic. Can you use GPT image gen or agy's nano banana to show me some more eccentric options? impeccable has a way for you to show me three options and then do more or less of what you showed
kept: The general design (three columns: chat list with branch tree, conversation, visuals panel with the limits row) stays; the world changes.

options.label: Riso Zine
options.thesis: Crush printed like a risograph zine: paper-light, two spot inks, and the branch you cut from a sentence printed in fluorescent pink.
materials: two spot inks with slight misregistration on pink only
options.viewport: Standard three columns. Pink marks every way into a branch: the highlighted words, the branch path in the chat list, the selected chat. Blue carries AI names, times and secondary marks.
options.signature: Overprinted fluorescent-pink highlight on branch words; the same ink draws the branch path in the left list.

raised.raise: Pink is reserved for branch paths and the current selection, like a course line that never decorates the terrain.
Hierarchy by type size and weight alone; messages are not boxed.
Flat, unmodulated ink: no halftone grain on working surfaces.
Every usage number shows when it was read.
The next chat is one key away and already loaded.

options.risk: A light, paper-like app breaks a dark-desktop habit; pink is loud; the misregistration must stay subtle or text looks blurry.

options.label: Transit Map
options.lineage: Vignelli's 1972 New York subway diagram; Beck's Tube map
options.thesis: Every chat is a line and every branch an interchange; each AI tool owns a line colour you learn in a day.
options.viewport: Standard three columns; the chat list's branch tree drawn as a small line diagram; line bullets (coloured discs with a letter) mark each chat's AI everywhere.
options.signature: The branch tree as a transit diagram with interchanges at branch points.
options.risk: Familiar: branches as coloured lines is the git-graph picture many developer tools use, so it can read as a git client. This was my top-ranked candidate.

options.label: Jet-Age Ticket
options.thesis: Each chat is a journey in a ticket wallet: facts in hairline-ruled fare boxes, and states that stamp themselves.
options.viewport: Standard three columns; navy left rail and headings; the right panel's facts in ruled boxes with tab-cap labels and carbon-purple numbers; states stamp themselves (HOLD for waiting, PASSED for tool runs, VOID for stopped replies).
options.case: Holds product clarity better than the roll (every state gets a stamped word you can read at a glance); loses on how much it feels like the owner's own world.
options.risk: Stamps and ruled boxes can tip into a travel costume; purple numbers next to navy need care.

options.label: Type Specimen
options.case: Loses both axes: type-foundry culture is not the owner's world, and a specimen's giant display letters fight a dense working screen.

options.label: Orienteering Map
options.case: Loses both axes: niche to the owner, and the terrain colours compete with chat content.
options.kept: One ink reserved for the active path.

options.label: Monochrome Product Page
options.case: Fused, it is the category standard the canon card already offers; it only ties on clarity.
options.kept: Every number shows its proof (when it was read).

options.label: Zoo Guide Map
options.case: Loses both axes: lobed shapes cannot hold three working columns, and its land colour is green (banned as the main colour).

options.label: Vertical Video Feed
options.case: Loses both axes: one item per screen cannot show the chat list, the chat and the visuals together.
options.kept: The next item is one step away and already loaded.

buildPath.note: The brief pins the mockup-led workflow.

canonCard.label: Keep the current look
canonCard.thesis: The category standard, played straight: charcoal and amber, as in style-2.
canonCard.risk: What most AI chat apps look like.
